about: Ambiguous local searches for tools/research_relevance_benchmark.py, with a fixed pool of search results per question (names are made up). 'about' says whether a result is about what was asked or about another meaning of a word in it. 'dev' is the owner's Omaha question, which the planner was written for, and the same results for the other meaning (getting rid of lawn weeds), added in round two so that a judge which simply drops lawn pages would be caught; 'heldout' was written at the same time and run afterwards, with nothing adjusted to it. Round one (2026-11-24) showed that the real model left the plan's list of other-meaning words empty for all seven; the result judge of round two was designed after seeing that, so 'heldout' is no longer unseen for round two. 'heldout2' was written after round one and before round two was run on any held-out question. Round two showed that results were not judged when the plan added no words of its own ('gaming mouse', 'glass pitcher'); round three judges them, so 'heldout2' is no longer unseen for round three. 'heldout3' was written after round two and before round three was run on any held-out question. The search engine is simulated: it ranks the pool by how many of the query's words a result contains, as a keyword search does, so the old pipeline gets what the question's words match.
